question: Was there anything in particular you paid attention to when writing Abel’s dialogue? Also, is the difference between the characters Abel calls by name and those he doesn’t mainly a matter of how close he is to them?
answer:
The thing I was careful about when writing him was making sure I didn't accidentally close both of his eyes.

There was a setting that he always kept one eye open because he was constantly on guard against assassination attempts, so I had to pay attention to that. There was even a time when someone pointed it out in the manuscript and I hurriedly fixed it. (laughs)

Also, until the end of Arc 7, I had to make sure the true reason Abel wanted to return to the Emperor’s throne wasn't revealed, so finding the right balance in how much of it to show was difficult.

Even Abel's poor attitude toward Subaru was part of his intention: he didn't want Subaru to include him among the things that were important to him.

But as the author, I needed readers to like Abel, while at the same time I couldn't have Subaru and Abel become too friendly… so that was difficult.

I think I consciously wrote him so that his treatment of Subaru was about one degree colder than his treatment of the other characters.

As for how he addresses people, I think importance, rather than familiarity, is more significant. He changes the way he treats people depending on who they are.

He's the type who operates according to efficiency and rationality rather than emotion, so I think his way of addressing people works the same way.
